A bigwig is an important, powerful, or highly influential person — someone who holds a top position, commands great authority, or carries significant weight in a particular field, organization, or society. Think of a CEO of a major company, a senior government minister, a legendary film director, or a top military general. Any of these people could be called a bigwig.

The word is almost always used in an informal context. You would say it in casual conversation or in journalism, but rarely in a formal report or official letter.
The Tone: Slightly Playful, Occasionally Irreverent

This is the most important nuance to understand about "bigwig." While the word acknowledges that someone is important, it does so with a slightly tongue-in-cheek, almost cheeky attitude. It subtly pokes fun at the grandeur or self-importance that powerful people often carry around themselves.

So when someone calls a person a bigwig, the tone is usually one of these three:

Neutral-to-admiring — simply acknowledging that someone is a big deal, with no hidden mockery.

"She's a bigwig in the world of tech investment."

Mildly humorous — treating the person's importance with a wink, as if to say "yes, yes, very impressive."

"The bigwigs flew in on private jets for the annual summit."

Gently mocking — suggesting the person is perhaps a little too impressed with their own status.

"The bigwigs upstairs made another decision without asking anyone who actually does the work."

Crucially, none of these tones are outright insulting. "Bigwig" does not mean a bad person or a corrupt one. It simply means a high-ranking person, described with a mild, knowing smirk.

A bigwig is almost always someone at the top of a hierarchy — whether that's a company, a government, an industry, a social circle, or any organized group. The key requirement is that they have real power, influence, or prestige that others recognize.

Here are some natural examples:

  • "The meeting was full of corporate bigwigs — presidents, vice presidents, and board members."
  • "A few Hollywood bigwigs attended the charity auction."
  • "He used to be a bigwig in the finance world before he retired."
  • "Don't worry about impressing the bigwigs — just do your job well."

Notice that you can use "bigwig" for a single person (a bigwig) or for a group (the bigwigs), and both are perfectly natural.

One subtle but important thing "bigwig" does is draw an invisible line between the powerful few and everyone else. When someone refers to "the bigwigs," they are almost always standing on the outside of that group — as an ordinary person looking at the people at the top. This is part of what gives the word its slightly irreverent flavor. It's rarely how powerful people describe themselves; it's how the rest of us describe them.

"Bigwig" implies genuine, significant importance — not minor or local fame. You wouldn't call the president of a small neighborhood club a bigwig (at least not sincerely). The word carries real weight. Bigwigs are people whose decisions affect many others, whose names are widely known within their sphere, and whose presence in a room changes the atmosphere.

Other informal words that work similarly to "bigwig" include: big shot, big cheese, heavyweight, top dog, VIP, mogul, and magnate. These all share the same core idea — a person of power and prominence — though each carries its own slight variation in tone. "Bigwig" sits comfortably among them as one of the most widely used and recognized.

A bigwig is a powerful, high-status, or influential person, described informally and with a gentle touch of humor. The word respects the person's importance while quietly winking at the whole idea of human self-importance. It's an everyday, versatile word you'll hear in conversation, news articles, and casual writing whenever someone wants to point out — with a knowing smile — that the big players are involved.
